idea: "What's Missing?" #2 (KITCHEN, at the pastel yellow fridge): Baby Ava's toddler crayon drawing of a red car on the fridge comes alive and bumps along – bump, bump, bump – but it has only ONE wheel ('Oh no! My car can't go!'); Ava points at the empty spot and asks the viewer 'What's missing? Hmm?' (2 s pause) – 'A wheel! A wheel! A round wheel!'; 'Magic crayon, draw with me!' – she draws a round wheel round and round; chorus 'Wheels go round and round!'; counting 'One wheel, two wheels! Yay!'; copy-me: roll your hands round and round. Loop: the hook framing again, the car complete with two wheels, bye-bye wave.
title: Oh No! My Car Can't Go! 🚗 What's Missing? | Learn with Baby Ava | Crayon Babies
description:
Oh no! Baby Ava's crayon car on the fridge can't go – bump, bump, bump! Something is missing… Can you spot it? Look closely, shout the answer, and help Ava fix her car with the Magic Crayon!

🎬 What happens in this video:
😮 "Oh no! My car can't go!" – bump, bump, bump!
🤔 "What's missing?" – look closely and shout the answer!
🚗 A wheel! A round wheel!
🖍️ "Magic crayon, draw with me!" – round and round
🙌 One wheel, two wheels – roll your hands round and round!
👋 Wheels go round! Bye bye, friends!

📚 Kids learn: spot what's missing • wheel • round • car • one, two

🎶 Voices only: children singing, humming and clapping with a soft hand drum – no other musical instruments.

A fun "What's Missing?" sing-along for toddlers and preschoolers: Baby Ava finds that her crayon car drawing has only one wheel, little viewers spot the missing part, and the Magic Crayon draws a round new wheel so the car can go again.
